Why are bacteria classified under kingdom monera? Give TWO reasons.
In the five-kingdom system, bacteria are unicellular prokaryotes. They have no membrane-bound nucleus and lack membrane-bound organelles.

Consider the given equation of decomposition of hydrogen peroxide by catalase enzyme.

$2\mathrm{H_2O_2}\xrightarrow{\mathrm{Catalase}}2\mathrm{H_2O}+\mathrm{O_2}$

The given graph shows the progression of this enzyme-catalysed reaction.

a. At what time does the rate of reaction begin to slow down? (1 mark)
b. Why does the rate of reaction become slow? (1 mark)

a. The oxygen curve starts to flatten at about 175 s.
b. As hydrogen peroxide is used up, its concentration falls and productive enzyme–substrate collisions become less frequent.

The given graph shows the breathing rate (breaths per minute) of an individual during and after exercise.

a. Locate the point on the graph where lactic acid production is the HIGHEST. (1 mark)
b. Why is the breathing rate of the individual higher during exercise between 10 to 12 minutes? Give any TWO reasons. (2 marks)

a. The intended estimate is around the peak during exercise, approximately 11 minutes. The graph measures breathing rate, so it does not establish the exact time of peak lactate production.
b. Active muscles require more oxygen for aerobic respiration and produce more carbon dioxide that ventilation helps remove.

The given diagram shows a normal blood sample and a sample from a patient with a blood disorder as seen under a microscope. Based on the information in the given diagram,

a. identify the blood disorder. (1 mark)
b. write ONE likely effect of the blood disorder on the patient. (1 mark)

a. Leukaemia is the disorder suggested by the excess of white blood cells in the comparison.
b. An increased risk of infection is one likely effect because abnormal white blood cells may not defend effectively against infection.

Justify how mitochondrial dysfunction, in a person with a genetic disorder, results in each of the given symptoms:

• Muscle weakness and fatigue (2 marks)
• Impaired brain function (2 marks)
• Impaired heart function (2 marks)

Mitochondrial dysfunction can reduce ATP supply. Skeletal muscles have less ATP available for repeated contractions, causing weakness and fatigue. Neurons have less energy to maintain ion gradients and transmit signals, impairing brain function. Cardiac muscle has less energy for sustained contractions, which can reduce pumping ability.

If a person breathes polluted air containing high levels of carbon monoxide, how would this affect the normal physiological function, and the composition of oxygen and carbon dioxide in expired air?

Carbon monoxide binds strongly to haemoglobin, reducing oxygen carriage and delivery to tissues. Reduced oxygen uptake and reduced aerobic metabolism could leave more oxygen and less carbon dioxide in expired air if other conditions were comparable. The table alone does not determine the direction or size of the changes because ventilation and exposure can also vary.

A patient with vitamin deficiencies is experiencing fatigue, weakened immune function and delayed wound healing. Based on the given symptoms,

i. name any TWO vitamins that are deficient in the patient. (2 marks)
ii. recommend any TWO dietary modifications that would help to overcome the vitamin deficiencies named in part ‘i’. (2 marks)
iii. justify your recommendations in part ‘ii’ with reference to each dietary modification. (2 marks)

One defensible pair is vitamins C and B₁₂. Add guava or citrus for vitamin C, which supports collagen formation and wound healing. Add B₁₂-fortified foods, eggs or dairy for vitamin B₁₂, which supports normal red blood cell formation. Deficiency can contribute to anaemia and fatigue. The symptoms alone do not identify two unique deficiencies.

The given graph shows the effect of exercise on heart rate in beats per minute (BPM) over time.

i. Based on the graph, how quickly does the heart rate recover after exercise? (2 marks)
ii. If a person with compromised cardiovascular health performed the same exercise, how might their heart rate and recovery time differ? (2 marks)
iii. If another person’s resting heart rate is 60 BPM instead of 72 BPM, how would their exercise-induced heart rate response compare to this graph? (2 marks)

i. Recovery starts around minute 12 and continues to minute 20, about eight minutes. The plotted heart rate is still above its initial value at the end.
ii. Heart rate may rise more for the same workload and may take longer to approach baseline.
iii. The second person starts from a lower baseline. A lower resting heart rate alone cannot determine their peak or recovery rate.
X: The given diagram shows a cell with four chromosomes. If this cell undergoes meiosis, then draw the chromosomes in the cell during prophase I, metaphase I and metaphase II.

Prophase I: draw four duplicated chromosomes paired into two homologous bivalents. Metaphase I: align the two bivalents at the equator. Metaphase II: in each haploid daughter cell, draw two duplicated chromosomes aligned singly at the equator.
A 55-year-old person sustained an injury to the frontal lobe of the brain following a road accident. In the given scenario, evaluate any THREE problems that will be experienced by this person.

Possible effects depend on the exact site. Examples include difficulty planning or making decisions, reduced impulse control or changes in social behaviour, and weakness or reduced voluntary movement if the primary motor cortex is affected.

In the given diagram of a human nephron, trace the pathway of blood with the help of arrows (→).

(Note: Do NOT show the pathway of the filtrate.)
Afferent arteriole → glomerular capillaries → efferent arteriole → peritubular capillaries or vasa recta → venules.

The given diagram represents a human hinge joint.

a. Identify the structure labelled as X. (1 mark)
b. Name the cells that make structure X. (1 mark)
c. Mention the role of structure X in the joint. (1 mark)

a. Articular cartilage.
b. Chondrocytes are the mature cartilage cells.
c. Articular cartilage provides a smooth surface that reduces friction and distributes load between the bones.

A substantial portion of a tropical forest was removed to construct a highway. Within a few years, populations of birds and insects in that area declined significantly. How does the human activity cause a decline in the population of birds and insects?
Forest clearance destroys and fragments habitat. Birds lose nesting sites and food, and insects lose host plants and shelter. Fewer individuals survive and reproduce, so populations decline.
6a

The given graph illustrates the variations in the amount of DNA in a cell during different stages of the cell cycle. Analyse any THREE stages represented in the given graph. Provide reasons for the changes in amount of DNA content to support your answer. (6 marks)

Stage I: DNA content is constant before replication (G₁). Stage II: DNA content doubles during S phase. Stage III: it remains doubled after DNA synthesis while the cell prepares to divide. Stage IV: the amount per daughter cell returns to its starting value when duplicated chromosomes are separated and the cell divides.
6b

i. Mention any FOUR physiological changes that would take place in the human body as a result of increased adrenaline level. (4 marks)
ii. Describe the importance of any TWO physiological changes mentioned in part (i) for exercise or emergency situation. (2 marks)

i. Heart rate increases, bronchioles dilate, the liver releases more glucose, and blood flow is redirected towards skeletal muscles.
ii. Faster circulation increases delivery of oxygen and fuel to active muscles. Increased glucose availability supplies fuel for respiration.
7a

i. Describe the structural adaptation of a wind-pollinated flower with reference to its petals, pollens, stamens and stigmas. (4 marks)
ii. Write the importance of any TWO structures (given in part i) adapted for pollination through wind. (2 marks)

i. Petals are small or inconspicuous. Pollen is light, dry and produced in large quantities. Stamens project out on flexible filaments. Stigmas are exposed and feathery.
ii. Exposed stamens release pollen into moving air. Feathery stigmas have a large area for intercepting airborne pollen.
7b
Describe continuous and discontinuous variations in humans. Give an example of human traits in each case to support your answer. (6 marks)

Continuous variation shows a measurable range with intermediate values, such as human height. Discontinuous variation consists of distinct categories without intermediate classes, such as ABO blood groups.
